title: Featuring with the Midriffs
summary: He describes the professional Midriffs band and its members and says he featured with them in clubs, unlike his own group with Robert Parker.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: So what band were you working with at this time? You had a band named the Midriffs, didn't you? It wasn't none of my band.

I was working with the Midriffs. Who was in that band? That was George Miller. He just recently died. He had three or four months ago. Maybe five. And Boots Alexis. Now what did he play? Oh, Boots? Yeah. He played the drums. And George Wilson, what did he play? He played an upright bass and he sung. Who else was in that band? They had Ellick Burrell. Ellick Burrell. Playing piano. He's now Duke Burrell. Duke Burrell. Yeah, he's in L.A. He changed his name. Yeah. No more Ellick. He's Duke Burrell now. And who else?
And you played piano? Well, after I joined the group.
Didn't join them but I would feature in different spots with them. What clubs?
Wherever they would be hired at. Yeah, if you played piano? Yeah.

So this was different from the group you had with Robert Parker? Yeah, altogether, yeah. This was a professional group. They were all professional musicians. Robert Parker and I was teaching them myself. But you've got to get off and learn other people's strategy too. If you want to be a musician, you're going to run into more than just one set. There were a variety of things and music to do if you don't.
So who's John- did John Woodrow work with you, with Robert Parker? A drummer named John Woodrow, you don't remember him?
Maybe he did, maybe he didn't. I worked with so many, you know, fellas that sometimes I don't take time to learn the name because the attitude didn't add up to what-
Yeah, and so you wouldn't call him.
I didn't remember the name, it didn't make sense because I knew I wasn't going to be using them or bother with him, you know.
